intro.text: You can get through Italy with English and pointing. *The trip is a different trip when you order, ask the way and chat at the market in Italian.*

items.title: A first trip
items.text: Rome, Florence, Venice. You want the basics that make every day easier: greetings, ordering, tickets, directions.

items.title: Two of you
items.text: A honeymoon or an anniversary. You learn together as a small group and practice on each other.

items.title: Family roots
items.text: You are visiting the town your family came from and want to talk with the people there.

items.title: Slow travel
items.text: A month in Puglia or a house in Tuscany. You want to shop, chat with the neighbors and feel at home.

items.title: Kids on the trip
items.text: Teens and kids can learn a few phrases too, at their own level, so they get more from the trip.

items.title: Spain or France?
items.text: Spanish for your trip works the same way, from Madrid to Mexico City. French too, for beginners.

chapters.body:
Everything is planned around your itinerary. If you are going to Naples and the Amalfi Coast, we use those places in the lessons: the ferry, the pizzeria, the lemon stand by the road.

You talk from the first lesson, so by the time you fly you have already said these things out loud.
chapters.imageAlt: A quiet cobbled street in a small Italian town

chapters.heading: Tell me your dates, and we plan *back from there*
chapters.body:
On the free 15-minute call you tell me where you are going, when you leave and where you are starting from. We count back from your departure and agree how many lessons fit.

Lessons are online, on video, so they work from anywhere in the US. If you live in the Atlanta metro area, we can also meet in person. Traveling as a couple or with friends? You can learn together as a small group.

I suggest two hours a week, so a few weeks before the trip is a good time to start. If your flight is sooner, tell me and we make the most of the time you have.
chapters.imageAlt: A passport, a folded map and a key on a stone floor

chapters.heading: Going to Italy? I can plan it *with you*
chapters.body: Besides the lessons, I put together trips to Italy around what you want to see, taste and do. Write to me, or ask on the free call.

items.q: I leave in three weeks. Is it too late?
items.a: No. Even a few lessons give you the phrases you will use every day. Tell me your date and I plan around it.

items.q: Do I need to live in Atlanta?
items.a: No. Travel lessons work online, on video, from anywhere in the US. In the Atlanta metro area we can also meet in person.

items.q: Can my partner and I learn together?
items.a: Yes. Couples, friends and families can learn as a small group and practice on each other.

items.q: How many lessons do I need?
items.a: It depends on your date and on where you start. On the free call we count back from your departure and agree a plan that fits.

items.q: Do you also help plan the trip itself?
items.a: Yes. Besides the lessons, I put together trips to Italy around what you want to see, taste and do. Ask on the free call, or write to me.

items.q: Can I learn Spanish for my trip?
items.a: Yes. Spanish travel lessons work the same way, built around your dates and your route, whether you are going to Spain or Latin America.

items.q: Can I learn French for a trip to France?
items.a: Yes. French is for beginners, and we build the lessons around your trip the same way.

items.q: How much do travel lessons cost?
items.a: [CONFIRM] There is no price list here because no two plans are the same: how many lessons, one-on-one or a group, in person or online. After the free call you get your price in writing, and you decide then.
